layers.name: Discover
layers.one: Agents find products and what each merchant's checkout supports.
layers.arch: Product feeds, well known capability files, MCP servers and Agent Cards tell agents what they can buy and how.

layers.name: Intent and mandate
layers.one: Proof of what the user allowed the agent to buy.
layers.arch: Token limits, signed open or closed mandates, or instructions the network holds. None defines a dispute process.

layers.name: Agent identity
layers.one: Lets a merchant tell a trusted agent from a bot.
layers.arch: Mostly RFC 9421 signed requests checked against a key directory, plus network registration or KYA tokens.

layers.name: Credential
layers.one: What pays, without handing card numbers to the agent.
layers.arch: Agentic network tokens, PSP scoped tokens, wallet accounts, stablecoin keys or bank account mandates such as UPI Reserve Pay.

layers.name: Rail
layers.one: How the money moves, and how fast and costly.
layers.arch: Card networks, real time bank rails, stablecoins on chain or Lightning. Each sets cost, speed and reversibility.

layers.name: Settle
layers.one: Money lands, and both sides reconcile the order.
layers.arch: Acquirers settle cards. Facilitators verify and settle HTTP 402 payments on chain, some batching many into one.

layers.name: Dispute
layers.one: Who refunds or absorbs a bad agent purchase.
layers.arch: Card reason codes written for human buyers, mandates offered as evidence, and no dispute path on chain rails.

usecases.name: Consumer checkout
usecases.one: A person's agent buys from a merchant with card or wallet.

usecases.name: B2B procurement
usecases.one: A business agent pays suppliers or invoices within limits a human set.

usecases.name: Machine pay per call
usecases.one: An agent pays per API call, tool call or page.

protocols.name: ACP
protocols.one: Simple REST checkout. It has gone quiet, and ChatGPT now sends buyers to retailer sites.
protocols.arch: Merchant feed, checkout sessions, then delegated payment returns a token capped by amount, merchant and expiry. Idempotency keys required. No agent identity scheme. Copilot Checkout used it for Stripe sellers at launch.
protocols.gaps: No signed user mandate, one time allowance only, no release since April.

params.P5: PSP scoped token or network token

protocols.name: UCP
protocols.owner: Google and Shopify, with Stripe and councils
protocols.one: The only checkout protocol with verified live consumer checkout in the last 90 days, via Google Universal Cart.
protocols.arch: Business profile and keys at a well known file, optional signed requests, checkout over REST, MCP, A2A or embedded. An optional AP2 mandate extension locks the session once negotiated.
protocols.gaps: Nothing tagged since August, both 2026 releases broke old versions. No B2B or pay per call.

params.P5: wallet account, PSP or network token

protocols.name: AP2
protocols.one: Signed mandates that prove what the user allowed, for purchases with or without them present.
protocols.arch: Open Checkout and Payment mandates set limits ahead, closed ones bind one cart. SD-JWT credentials with the agent key bound in. Transport left to UCP or A2A.
protocols.gaps: No release since April. Disputes out of scope. Signatures can sit on manipulated choices.

params.P11: not defined, runs inside UCP or A2A

protocols.name: A2A
protocols.one: Messaging between agents across companies. Commerce comes only through extensions such as x402.
protocols.arch: Signed Agent Cards for discovery and long running tasks. The x402 extension adds payment states and an append only receipts list, but has seen little work.
protocols.gaps: No commerce meaning in core. Extension has no spend limits or mandate link.

params.P1: machine to machine or not present

protocols.name: MCP
protocols.full: Model Context Protocol, WebMCP and Shop MCP
protocols.one: How agents call tools. Shopify runs live checkout on it, and paid tools wrap x402 or MPP.
protocols.arch: Stateless spec with no payment primitive. Shop MCP completes checkout only after the shopper confirms. AWS AgentCore pays for MCP tools over x402 and MPP.
protocols.gaps: No payment object, no mandate, no standard human confirmation for paid tool calls.

params.P1: human present or machine to machine

protocols.name: Web Bot Auth
protocols.full: IETF Web Bot Auth over RFC 9421
protocols.owner: IETF working group, Cloudflare and Google authors
protocols.one: Signed requests that prove which agent called. ChatGPT's browser already signs with it.
protocols.arch: Agent publishes keys at a well known address and signs each request. Verifiers fetch the directory and check the signature. Proves the agent, not the user's consent.
protocols.gaps: Not yet an RFC. Card network tags differ from the draft's single tag.

protocols.name: Visa TAP
protocols.one: Visa's agent identity check, now in a live B2B invoice pilot with BILL and Billtrust.
protocols.arch: Registered agents sign each request with RFC 9421 and a browse or pay tag. Merchant or CDN verifies against a Visa hosted key directory and a replay cache.
protocols.gaps: No versioned spec, sample repo idle, tags differ from the IETF draft.

params.P3: signed HTTP requests, network registered agent

protocols.name: Verifiable Intent
protocols.one: A signed record of what the cardholder asked for, shown in parts to each party.
protocols.arch: Chained SD-JWT layers bound to device and agent keys. The network sees payment data, the merchant sees checkout data. Fields align to AP2.
protocols.gaps: Still a first draft with one maintainer and no verified production use.

protocols.name: KYAPay and KYA
protocols.full: Know Your Agent tokens and framework
protocols.owner: Skyfire draft, Ant, Mastercard and Visa framework
protocols.one: A trusted issuer vouches for the agent and its human in a signed token.
protocols.arch: KYAPay carries identity and payment claims in JWTs sent in a request header. The cross network KYA framework has no spec or timeline.
protocols.gaps: Individual draft only. The trusted issuer list is out of scope.

params.P1: not present or machine to machine

protocols.name: FIDO, EMVCo, OpenID
protocols.full: Standards body work on agent identity and intent
protocols.one: Where mandate and agent authentication standards are expected to settle. No public draft yet.
protocols.arch: FIDO groups seeded with AP2 and Verifiable Intent, chaired by Mastercard and Visa for payments. EMVCo drafted intent services and is exploring agent checks. AuthZEN covers approvals.
protocols.gaps: No timeline from FIDO. EMVCo text seen only through trade press.

protocols.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce
protocols.one: Gives each agent its own Visa token after a passkey. Live, with volume Visa calls limited.
protocols.arch: Token provisioned through Visa Token Service, instructions sent as an encrypted payload. Connect accepts TAP, MPP, ACP and UCP. No agentic volume published.
protocols.gaps: No agentic fee or volume disclosed. Cardholders answer for enrolled agents under Visa rules.

protocols.name: Agent Pay
protocols.full: Mastercard Agent Pay and Agent Pay for Machines
protocols.one: Agentic Mastercard tokens for registered agents. Live in Shop Pay and several markets, volumes small.
protocols.arch: Agent registers, signs requests through Web Bot Auth, and pays with an agentic token in the normal card form. Issuer authorises, with a passkey where needed.
protocols.gaps: No GA statement or agent liability rule found. Machines product has no real money.

params.P3: network registered agent, signed HTTP requests

protocols.name: Amex ACE
protocols.one: Promises agent error cover, not yet live. Intent Intelligence has no live integrations.
protocols.arch: Intent Intelligence, published 2026-10-13, carries the purchase intent registered agents send Amex. Agent Purchase Protection is promised, not yet available.
protocols.gaps: No live integration yet. Protection terms and developer kit status not confirmed.

protocols.name: Stripe SPT
protocols.full: Stripe Shared Payment Tokens and Link
protocols.one: A scoped grant of the buyer's saved payment method to one seller, capped and revocable.
protocols.arch: Limits on currency, amount and expiry. Stripe may ride Visa or Mastercard agentic tokens underneath. Still under preview terms. Link balance spends USDC through a card.
protocols.gaps: No agent signature in the token flow. Link makes users answer for agent purchases.

protocols.name: x402
protocols.one: Pay per web request with stablecoins. Live, small, and down sharply since August.
protocols.arch: Server answers 402 with terms, client signs a stablecoin payment and retries, the server verifies, serves, then settles through a facilitator. Upto and batch settlement are merged.
protocols.gaps: No protocol refund or dispute path. Papers show unpaid service and paid but denied outcomes.

protocols.name: MPP
protocols.one: Pay per web request across many methods, from stablecoins to cards. Much smaller on chain.
protocols.arch: Charge, session and subscription intents. Methods include Tempo, Stripe, Lightning and Solana, with no ACH. Card payments settle off chain and are not counted.
protocols.gaps: IETF draft expired without working group adoption.

params.P5: stablecoin key, PSP token or card
params.P7: final on chain, chargeback on card

protocols.name: UPI agents
protocols.one: Users approve one spending limit per merchant, then the agent orders without repeated PIN prompts.
protocols.arch: UPI Reserve Pay blocks funds for several debits under a user approved limit. Piloted on Claude with Zomato, Swiggy and Zepto for a small group.
protocols.gaps: A wider agent protocol is reported, not confirmed. Liability and limits pending.

protocols.name: Pix agents
protocols.full: Pix agent payments through Iniciador MCP
protocols.owner: Banco Central do Brasil rail, Iniciador agent layer
protocols.one: Agents start Pix payments, and the user approves each one by device biometric.
protocols.arch: Iniciador's MCP server lets bank and fintech agents start Pix payments. Pix Automatico is a live recurring mandate rail on its own.
protocols.gaps: Launch status unstated and no volume disclosed.

protocols.name: Alipay and AMP
protocols.full: Alipay AI Pay and Ant AMP
protocols.one: The largest reported base, with explicit user approval for every payment. Figures are self reported.
protocols.arch: AI Pay installs into agents after an identity check. AI Wallet sits between user and agent. Ant's AMP runs on Alipay+ wallets.
protocols.gaps: Vendor figures only. AMP has no disclosed volumes or go live dates.

flows.name: Token checkout
flows.one: The agent never sees the card. A wallet or network hands the merchant a scoped token.
flows.arch: Discovery file or feed, signed agent request, buyer confirmation, then a single use network or PSP token charged through the merchant's own PSP. Disputes follow card reason codes.

steps.msg: Reads merchant profile and catalog
Signs request with registered agent key
Confirms total and payment method
Issues single use network token
Authorises token on card network
Sends order events to the agent
Handles disputes under card reason codes

flows.name: Signed mandate
flows.one: The user signs limits ahead, the agent signs the cart, and both become evidence.
flows.arch: Open mandate on a trusted surface binds the agent key. The agent signs a closed mandate over the cart hash. Credential provider checks both before issuing a token.

steps.msg: Signs open mandate on trusted surface
Builds cart with the merchant
Signs closed mandate bound to cart
Checks agent key in the mandate
Verifies mandates and issues payment token
Verifies bindings and returns signed receipts
Keeps mandates and receipts as evidence

flows.name: HTTP 402 pay per call
flows.one: The server asks for payment in its reply, and the agent pays and retries.
flows.arch: A 402 reply carries the price. The wallet checks its cap, signs and retries. The server verifies, serves, then settles through a facilitator. Payment is final.

steps.msg: Calls a paid API or tool
Replies 402 with price and payee
Checks the spend cap
Signs stablecoin payment authorisation
Verifies the signed payment for the server
Serves the data, settles, returns receipt
No protocol dispute path, refund by agreement

params.name: Initiator presence
params.why: Sets whether step up is possible and how disputes are judged.

params.name: Payer type
params.why: Picks the legal regime, consumer rules or business contract.

params.name: Agent identity method
values: CDN verified bot, Direct or Intermediary
params.why: Lets a merchant tell a trusted agent from a bot.

params.name: Mandate type
params.why: Decides what proof exists that the user agreed.

params.name: Credential
params.why: Decides who can see and reuse the payment detail.

params.name: Rail
params.why: Sets cost, speed, reach and reversibility.

params.name: Finality
params.why: Decides who absorbs a bad purchase.

params.name: Merchant of record
params.who: Contract, set by the agent platform's checkout
params.why: Owns tax, refunds and customer service.

params.name: Dispute path
params.why: Card reason codes were written for human buyers.

params.name: Liability holder
values: cardholder for an enrolled agent on Visa
params.why: The open question that slows adoption.

params.name: Transport
params.why: Sets who must change their stack.

params.name: Crypto primitive
params.why: Decides what can be verified offline and by whom.

params.name: Discovery
params.why: An agent cannot buy what it cannot find.

params.name: Jurisdiction
params.why: Consent, refund and liability rules differ by country.

params.name: Merchant authenticity check
params.why: Agents have paid fake stores in tests. P3 checks only the agent.

params.name: Agent access policy
params.why: Merchants now publish opposite rules on which agents may browse or buy.

params.name: Checkout location
values: merchant site through an agent browser
params.why: Decides where the buyer's final page lives, which transport alone does not say.

params.name: Consent capture surface
values: trusted surface such as a wallet or OS
params.why: Decides who can prove consent. A bot signature is not consent.

params.name: Agent signal at authorization
values: agentic network token with agent header
PSP token riding an agentic token
params.who: Network and PSP, agent platform picks
params.why: Stored cards hide the agent, so the issuer cannot apply agent risk controls.

params.name: Buyer identity and account linking
params.who: Merchant offers, agent platform chooses, user consents
params.why: Keeps loyalty and the customer record with the merchant.

params.name: Mandate enforcement point
params.why: Tells the merchant which checks it must run and which it cannot.

vars.name: Spend limit
vars.typical: per payment, per period, per merchant
vars.why: Caps loss when the agent errs. Only the platform or network sees every merchant.

vars.name: Expiry
vars.typical: minutes to months, and different at each layer
vars.why: Shorter expiry lowers the stolen credential window. Lifetimes differ by layer.
vars.who: Protocol and the issuer of each layer

vars.name: Scope
vars.why: Stops the right amount being spent on the wrong thing.

vars.name: Revocation
vars.why: A mandate must not outlive the user's intent.

vars.name: Step up threshold
vars.typical: amount or risk score that forces a passkey or approval

vars.name: Idempotency key and retries
vars.why: Stops double charges when an agent retries.

vars.name: Order events
vars.why: The agent must tell the user what happened.

vars.name: Evidence retention
vars.typical: mandate, cart, agent id, logs, kept for the rail's dispute window, then deleted

vars.name: Fees
vars.typical: card fees, gas, protocol fee, agent platform fee per sale
vars.why: Decides which use cases pay off.

vars.name: Latency budget
vars.why: Pay per call needs sub second settlement.

vars.name: Pre signing context capture
vars.typical: none, cart only, cart plus offers and ranking shown
vars.why: A valid signature can sit on a manipulated choice.

vars.name: Agent model and version recorded
vars.typical: not recorded, in the mandate, in the receipt
vars.why: Model updates change what agents buy, and users rarely notice.

vars.name: Revocation evidence
vars.typical: user record, platform signed notice, issuer or network registry
vars.why: A bank now makes customers prove they revoked an agent.

vars.name: Settlement mode
vars.typical: per payment, metered session, batched with upto or batch settlement, or authorize then capture, through a network, PSP, facilitator or wallet provider
vars.why: Cost, latency and concentration sit in how and through whom payments settle.

vars.name: Minimum ticket
vars.typical: smallest amount the PSP or facilitator will settle per payment
vars.why: Decides which use cases are possible at all, such as pay per call.

vars.name: Own agent completed share
vars.why: Our proposed threshold, not sourced. Above 3% for two months, build the gateway.
